questions.stem: Which of the following is otherwise known as grain alcohol?
questions.explanation: Ethanol (C2H5OH) is commonly called grain alcohol because it is produced by fermentation of grains.

questions.stem: Alcohols have higher boiling points than alkanes of similar molecular weight because

options.A: Oxygen is present in alcohols which is deficient in alkanes
options.B: Strong ionic bonding is present in alcohols while covalent bonding is present in alkanes
options.C: Interaction between oxygen of the hydroxyl group with other molecules of alcohols which is absent in alkanes
options.D: Alkanes are largely hydrocarbons which mostly are in gaseous states

questions.explanation: Alcohols form intermolecular hydrogen bonds through their -OH group, significantly raising boiling points compared to non-polar alkanes.

questions.stem: The carbon atom bonded to a hydroxyl group is called
questions.explanation: A carbon directly bonded to an -OH group is called a carbinol carbon.

questions.stem: Glycols have _____ hydroxyl group(s).
questions.explanation: Glycols (diols) by definition contain two hydroxyl (-OH) groups.

questions.stem: Which of the alcohols is otherwise known as wood spirit?
questions.explanation: Methanol (CH3OH) is called wood spirit because it was originally obtained by the destructive distillation of wood.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT another name for 2-propanol?
questions.explanation: 2-propanol is known as isopropanol, isopropyl alcohol, and rubbing alcohol. Vinylpropanol is not a name for it.

questions.stem: Alcohols react with active metals (Na, K, etc.) to produce _____ gas.
questions.explanation: Alcohols react with active metals to release hydrogen gas: 2ROH + 2Na -> 2RONa + H2.

questions.stem: Which of these chemicals would you recommend for a person who has dry skin?
questions.explanation: Glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) is a humectant commonly used in skin moisturizers.

questions.stem: The green engine coolant in an automobile radiator will likely contain one of these
questions.explanation: Ethylene glycol (ethane-1,2-diol) is the main component of antifreeze/engine coolant.

questions.stem: An example of a polyhydric alcohol is
questions.explanation: Cellulose contains multiple hydroxyl groups per monomer unit, making it a polyhydric compound.

questions.stem: The formation of ethylene glycol from ethylene is an example of
questions.explanation: Converting ethylene (alkene) to ethylene glycol involves oxidation using OsO4 or peracids.

questions.stem: Which of these is a secondary alcohol?
questions.explanation: A secondary alcohol has the -OH group on a carbon bonded to two other carbons. CH3(CH3)CHOH (isopropanol) fits this.

questions.stem: An example of a compound that contains a carbonyl group is
questions.explanation: Formaldehyde (H2CO) contains a C=O carbonyl group.

questions.stem: One mole of NaBH4 reacts with 1 mole of acetone to give, after treatment with aqueous acid
questions.explanation: NaBH4 reduces ketones to secondary alcohols. Acetone is reduced to 2-propanol.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT true about alcohols?

options.A: The melting and boiling points of butanol is higher than ethanol
options.B: Ethanol is more soluble in water than octanol
options.C: Hexanol is more miscible with water than Methanol
options.D: The boiling point of methanol is higher than that of ethane

questions.explanation: Methanol is more miscible with water than hexanol due to its smaller hydrophobic chain.

questions.stem: LAH reacts with glyoxal to give
questions.explanation: LAH fully reduces both aldehyde groups of glyoxal (OHCCHO) to give ethylene glycol.

questions.stem: The correct name for the diol structure shown is
questions.explanation: The structure shows a hexane chain with OH at positions 2 and 5, ethyl at 4, and methyl at 3.

questions.stem: Which of these will NOT mix with water in all proportions?
questions.explanation: Nonanol has a long nonpolar chain that overcomes the polar -OH group's ability to hydrogen bond with water.

questions.stem: LAH reacts with H2CCHC(O)H to give
questions.explanation: LAH selectively reduces the aldehyde without saturating the alkene double bond, giving an allylic alcohol.

questions.stem: H2 in the presence of Raney Ni catalyst reacts with an unsaturated aldehyde to give
questions.explanation: H2/Raney Ni reduces both the C=C and C=O bonds of an unsaturated aldehyde to give a saturated alcohol.

questions.stem: Which of these is a tertiary alcohol?
questions.explanation: A tertiary alcohol has the -OH group on a carbon bonded to three other carbon groups.

questions.stem: Alcohol can be prepared by all the following ways EXCEPT

options.B: Addition of bromine water to alkene
options.D: Addition of Grignard reagent to alkene

questions.explanation: Grignard reagents react with carbonyl compounds, not directly with alkenes, to form alcohols.

questions.stem: Which of these compounds has no carbonyl group present in it?
questions.explanation: Nitriles contain a C≡N group, not a carbonyl (C=O) group.

questions.stem: In a carbonyl group, the oxygen atom is said to be
questions.explanation: The oxygen in a carbonyl group is electron-rich (nucleophilic) due to lone pairs.

questions.stem: Why should you not add aqueous acid in the first step of NaBH4/LAH reduction of a ketone?

options.A: It will reduce a ketone to a primary alcohol instead
options.C: Acid will have reacted with the reagent before the carbonyl has any chance to undergo reduction

questions.explanation: Both NaBH4 and LAH are destroyed by protic acids before they can reduce the carbonyl compound.

questions.stem: Reactions involving LAH must always be in inert solvents because

options.A: LAH is inactive in any other solvents
options.B: Reactive solvents produce large side reaction products
options.C: LAH will react with solvents having acidic hydrogen atoms

questions.explanation: LAH reacts vigorously with protic solvents (water, alcohols), destroying the reagent.

questions.stem: Why prefer LAH over NaBH4 as reducing agent for carbonyl group?

options.B: NaBH4 is too slow to reduce carbonyl group
options.C: NaBH4 is not as selective as LAH

questions.explanation: LAH is a much stronger reducing agent than NaBH4 and can reduce a wider range of functional groups.

questions.stem: Products of reaction of CH3CH2C(O)OCH3 with LAH followed by acid?
questions.explanation: LAH reduces esters to two alcohols: the acyl portion gives 1-propanol and the alkoxy portion gives methanol.

questions.stem: Which reagent gives a saturated alcohol with an unsaturated aldehyde?
questions.explanation: H2/Raney Nickel reduces both C=C and C=O bonds, yielding a fully saturated alcohol.

questions.stem: What is X in the reaction of CH3CH=CHCH2CHO with 1. NaBH4, 2. H3O+?
questions.explanation: NaBH4 selectively reduces the aldehyde without affecting the alkene, giving an allylic alcohol.

questions.stem: What is the function of H3O+ in RMgX reactions with carbonyl compounds?

options.A: To produce magnesium salt of an alkoxide ion
options.B: To convert the alkoxide ion to alcohol
options.C: To neutralize the alkaline reaction medium
options.D: To reduce the carbonyl group to alcohol

questions.explanation: After Grignard addition, aqueous acid (H3O+) protonates the alkoxide to give the alcohol.

questions.stem: Reactions involving RMgX must be in inert solvents because

options.A: Solvents with acidic protons will destroy the reagent before it reacts with the carbonyl compound
options.C: RMgX is very reactive toward solvents having acidic protons
options.D: RMgX becomes deactivated upon contact with reactive solvents

questions.explanation: Grignard reagents are destroyed by protic solvents via proton transfer.

questions.stem: Which of these groups does NOT possess an acidic proton?
questions.explanation: An ether group (-O-CH3) has no O-H or N-H bond and thus no acidic proton.

questions.stem: Products of reacting methyl propanoate with 2 equiv. CH3CH2MgCl, then acid?
questions.explanation: Two equivalents of Grignard with an ester gives a tertiary alcohol. Methanol is released.

questions.stem: What is the product of 1 equivalent of Grignard with an ester, acyl chloride or carboxylate salt?
questions.explanation: One equivalent of Grignard with an ester gives a ketone intermediate.

questions.stem: Which reagent will oxidize primary alcohols directly to aldehydes?
questions.explanation: Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes without over-oxidizing to carboxylic acids.

questions.stem: Oxidation of secondary alcohols in either acidic or basic conditions will give
questions.explanation: Secondary alcohols are oxidized to ketones.

questions.stem: What product from oxidizing tertiary alcohol with dichromate or permanganate?
questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols cannot be oxidized by Cr2O7^2- or KMnO4 - no H on the carbinol carbon.

questions.stem: Identify X and Y as different classes of alcohols (X = tertiary, Y = secondary)

options.A: X is 2o alcohol, Y is 3o alcohol
options.B: X is 2o alcohol, Y is 1o alcohol
options.C: X is 3o alcohol, Y is 2o alcohol
options.D: X is 3o alcohol, Y is 1o alcohol

questions.explanation: X has three carbon substituents on the carbinol carbon (tertiary); Y has two (secondary).

questions.stem: A terminal ketone is otherwise known as
questions.explanation: When a carbonyl group is at the end of a carbon chain (terminal), it is an aldehyde.

questions.stem: The carbonyl group is capable of undergoing the following reactions EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Carbonyl groups undergo oxidation, reduction, and nucleophilic addition but not elimination reactions directly.

questions.stem: The preservative used for biological specimens contains
questions.explanation: Formalin, used to preserve biological specimens, is an aqueous solution of methanal (formaldehyde).

questions.stem: To prepare formalin I would dissolve
questions.explanation: Formalin is a 37% w/w solution: 37 g formaldehyde dissolved in 63 g water.

questions.stem: A pure source of methanal is
questions.explanation: Trioxane is a cyclic trimer of formaldehyde that depolymerizes to release pure methanal.

questions.stem: Acetone is used in organic laboratories for cleaning glassware because it is
questions.explanation: Acetone's polarity dissolves organic residues and its high volatility means it evaporates quickly.

questions.stem: Which of these could wood varnishes contain?
questions.explanation: Methyl ethyl ketone (2-butanone) is a common solvent used in wood varnishes and lacquers.

questions.stem: CH3CHO reacts first with ethyllithium then with dilute acid to give
questions.explanation: Ethyllithium adds to acetaldehyde to give an alkoxide, which is protonated to butan-2-ol.

questions.stem: Lithium reacts with n-butyl chloride to give
questions.explanation: Organolithium compounds are made by reacting lithium metal with alkyl halides (RX + 2Li -> RLi + LiX).

questions.stem: Formaldehyde (HCHO) reacts first with CH3MgCl and then with dilute acid to give a
questions.explanation: Grignard addition to formaldehyde gives a primary alcohol after workup.

questions.stem: The oxidation of CH3CH2OH with acidic dichromate (Cr2O7^2-) gives
questions.explanation: Primary alcohols are fully oxidized by acidic dichromate to carboxylic acids.

questions.stem: CH3CH2OH reacts with pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) to give
questions.explanation: PCC is a mild oxidant that stops oxidation of primary alcohols at the aldehyde stage.

questions.stem: PBr3 reacts with ethanol to give
questions.explanation: PBr3 converts alcohols to alkyl bromides: 3ROH + PBr3 -> 3RBr + P(OH)3.

questions.stem: Thionyl chloride, ClS(O)Cl, reacts with isopropyl alcohol to give
questions.explanation: SOCl2 replaces the -OH of secondary alcohols with -Cl.

questions.stem: Isopropyl alcohol reacts with hot concentrated H2SO4 to give
questions.explanation: Hot concentrated H2SO4 dehydrates alcohols via elimination to give alkenes.

questions.stem: Aldehydes have _____ boiling points than alcohols of comparable molecular weight.
questions.explanation: Alcohols can hydrogen bond with each other; aldehydes cannot. So alcohols have higher boiling points.

questions.stem: Acetone is the common name for
questions.explanation: Acetone's IUPAC name is propan-2-one (2-propanone), the simplest ketone.

questions.stem: Which material is most reactive toward nucleophilic addition?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones; less steric hindrance and more electrophilic carbonyl.

questions.stem: The oxidation of 1-propanol with chromic acid yields
questions.explanation: Chromic acid fully oxidizes primary alcohols to carboxylic acids.

questions.stem: The oxidation of 2-propanol with chromic acid yields
questions.explanation: Chromic acid oxidizes secondary alcohols to ketones.

questions.stem: The oxidation of 1-propanol with PCC gives
questions.explanation: PCC selectively oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes without proceeding to carboxylic acids.

questions.stem: The oxidation of _____ with ozone followed by reduction with (CH3)2S yields one product, 1,5-pentanedial.
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis of cyclopentene cleaves the ring to give a single dialdehyde (1,5-pentanedial).

questions.stem: The acid-catalyzed hydration of cyclodecyne yields
questions.explanation: Markovnikov hydration of an internal cyclic alkyne gives a cyclic ketone.

questions.stem: Reduction of acetic acid with Li(tri-tert-butoxy)AlH yields
questions.explanation: The bulky Li(tri-tert-butoxy)AlH is a hindered reducing agent that stops at the aldehyde stage.

questions.stem: The reaction of acetyl chloride with excess Grignard reagent followed by acidification yields
questions.explanation: Excess Grignard with an acid chloride first gives a ketone, then adds again to give a tertiary alcohol.

questions.stem: Lithium dimethylcuprate (Gilman reagent) reacts with acetyl chloride to give
questions.explanation: Gilman reagents react with acid chlorides to give ketones and stop there.

questions.stem: The cyanide ion -C≡N reacts with a ketone to give
questions.explanation: CN- adds to the carbonyl of a ketone to form a cyanohydrin (hydroxy nitrile).

questions.stem: The acid-catalyzed addition of water to formaldehyde gives
questions.explanation: Water adds to formaldehyde to give a geminal diol (hydrate): HCHO + H2O -> CH2(OH)2.

questions.stem: The acid-catalyzed addition of 2 mol of alcohol to 1 mol of aldehyde yields
questions.explanation: Two equivalents of alcohol react with an aldehyde to give a full acetal.

questions.stem: Ammonia reacts with an aldehyde to give an
questions.explanation: Ammonia condenses with aldehydes to form imines (Schiff bases).

questions.stem: The reaction of a Wittig reagent with ketones gives
questions.explanation: The Wittig reaction converts a C=O group into a C=C (alkene).

questions.stem: Silver ion Ag+ reacts with aldehydes to form
questions.explanation: Tollens' test: Ag+ is reduced by aldehydes to Ag metal, depositing a silver mirror.

questions.stem: Dimethylamine reacts with a ketone to give an
questions.explanation: Secondary amines condense with ketones to give enamines (C=C-N<).

questions.stem: Carbocations are

options.A: Carbon atoms with a negative charge
options.B: Carbon atoms with a positive charge
options.D: Any atom with a positive charge

questions.explanation: Carbocations are carbon species bearing a positive charge, with only 6 electrons around carbon.

questions.stem: A _____ carbocation has the greatest stability.
questions.explanation: Tertiary carbocations are most stable due to hyperconjugation and inductive donation from three alkyl groups.

questions.stem: Carbocations are stabilized by adjacent groups that _____ the carbocation.
questions.explanation: Electron-donating groups stabilize the positive charge on carbocations.

questions.stem: What is the name of the compound with carbonyl groups at positions 2 and 5 of heptane?
questions.explanation: Ketone groups at carbons 2 and 5 of a 7-carbon chain give 2,5-heptanedione.

questions.stem: The correct name for a keto-aldehyde with a methyl branch at C3 and keto at C6 of a heptane chain is
questions.explanation: The compound has an aldehyde at C1 and a ketone at C6, with a methyl at C3.

questions.stem: What is responsible for the high boiling points of aldehydes and ketones?

options.B: Intermolecular forces of attraction between molecules

questions.explanation: Aldehydes and ketones have high dipole moments; polar interactions raise their boiling points.

questions.stem: The Markovnikov rule states that a hydrogen atom bonds to the carbon atom that already is bonded to _____ hydrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: Markovnikov's rule: H adds to the carbon with more H atoms already attached.

questions.stem: Carbocations undergo rearrangement reactions

options.D: For all of the above reasons

questions.explanation: Carbocation rearrangements occur via hydride or methyl shifts to reach more stable carbocations.

questions.stem: Alkenes undergo an acid-catalyzed addition of water to give
questions.explanation: Acid-catalyzed hydration of alkenes gives alcohols.

questions.stem: Borane reacts with alkenes

options.A: To give the anti-Markovnikov addition product

questions.explanation: Hydroboration is a concerted syn addition that gives anti-Markovnikov products.

questions.stem: Diols are synthesized by reacting an alkene with
questions.explanation: OsO4 adds across an alkene double bond in concerted syn addition to give a cis-diol.

questions.stem: Ozone reacts with 2,3-dimethyl-2-butene to give
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis of this symmetrical internal alkene gives only one ketone product (acetone x 2).

questions.stem: The rapid conversion between an enol and its keto form is called
questions.explanation: Keto-enol tautomerism is the rapid interconversion between the keto and enol forms.

questions.stem: The solubility of aldehydes and ketones in water is due to

options.B: Polar interaction and hydrogen bonding between water and the carbonyl molecules
options.D: Dispersion and Van der Waal forces only

questions.explanation: Carbonyl oxygen forms hydrogen bonds with water, and dipole-dipole interactions also contribute.

questions.stem: Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones because

options.A: The carbonyl carbon in aldehydes is more polar
options.B: The carbonyl carbon in ketones is more sterically hindered from nucleophilic attack
options.C: The carbonyl carbon in aldehydes is terminal
options.D: The tetrahedral structure of aldehydes has higher potential energy

questions.explanation: In ketones, two alkyl groups flank the carbonyl, creating steric hindrance. Aldehydes have only one.

questions.stem: The intermediate formed during ozonolysis is called
questions.explanation: During ozonolysis, a molozonide rearranges to an ozonide intermediate.

questions.stem: Reaction of alkene with ozone in the presence of hydrogen peroxide will produce
questions.explanation: Depending on the alkene structure, ozonolysis with oxidative workup can give acids, ketones, or mixtures.

questions.stem: Ozonolysis is very important in chemistry because

options.B: It can be used to characterize complex molecules
options.C: It takes place at room temperature
options.D: It is a means of reducing complex molecules

questions.explanation: Ozonolysis cleaves double bonds predictably, allowing chemists to identify molecular fragments.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a way of preparing aldehydes and ketones?
questions.explanation: Amination reactions produce amines, not aldehydes or ketones.

questions.stem: What is the product of oxidizing cycloheptanone with KMnO4/OH-/H+?
questions.explanation: Vigorous oxidation of a cyclic ketone with KMnO4 opens the ring to give a linear dicarboxylic acid.

questions.stem: Which of these has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Butanol can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds, giving it the highest boiling point among the four.

questions.stem: Product from hydration of CH3C≡CCH2CH3 using mercury salt?
questions.explanation: Hg(II)-catalyzed hydration of an unsymmetrical internal alkyne gives a mixture of both possible ketones.

questions.stem: Aromatic ketones are prepared by
questions.explanation: Friedel-Crafts acylation uses an acyl chloride + AlCl3 to introduce a ketone group onto an aromatic ring.

questions.stem: Cyanohydrins hydrolysed in the presence of acid produce

options.A: Compounds with both hydroxyl and carboxylic groups

questions.explanation: Cyanohydrin hydrolysis converts -CN to -COOH, giving an alpha-hydroxy acid.

questions.stem: What is the product of the reaction of water with ketones?
questions.explanation: Water adds to a ketone to form a geminal diol (hydrate).

questions.stem: What is the final product of the reaction of alcohol with aldehyde called?
questions.explanation: The reaction of an aldehyde with two equivalents of alcohol gives an acetal.

questions.stem: Hexene and 2-hexene are:
questions.explanation: Hexene and 2-hexene have the same formula but the double bond is at different positions.

questions.stem: Chain isomers are compounds that have the same molecular formula but differ in
questions.explanation: Chain isomers differ in the carbon skeleton (branching), i.e., bonding arrangement.

questions.stem: How many structural isomers can you write for C5H12?
questions.explanation: C5H12 has 3 structural isomers: n-pentane, isopentane (2-methylbutane), and neopentane.

questions.stem: How many saturated cycles can you write from C5H10?
questions.explanation: C5H10 cycloalkane isomers: cyclopentane, methylcyclobutane, and dimethylcyclopropane - 3 total.

questions.stem: The suffix of CH3-CH2-CH2-CH=C(CH2CH3)-COOH is
questions.explanation: Longest chain with COOH has 6 carbons; double bond at position 2 = hex-2-enoic acid.

questions.stem: CH2=CHCl is
questions.explanation: CH2=CHCl is vinyl chloride (chloroethene), monomer of PVC.

questions.stem: The different parts of a systematic name include all of these EXCEPT
questions.explanation: A systematic name has prefix, principal chain, and suffix. 'Straight chain' is not a formal naming component.

questions.stem: Melting point of members of carboxylic acid homologous series

options.C: Even carbon acids have higher melting points than their immediate higher and lower members

questions.explanation: Odd-even alternation: even-carbon carboxylic acids pack more efficiently.

questions.stem: Melting points of structural isomers of carboxylic acids are _____ their normal chain counterpart
questions.explanation: Branched-chain isomers cannot pack as efficiently, resulting in lower melting points.

questions.stem: Carboxylic acids have higher boiling points due to
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids form strong hydrogen-bonded dimers, dramatically raising their boiling points.

questions.stem: Hell-Volard-Zelinsky reaction is
questions.explanation: HVZ reaction selectively brominates the alpha carbon of carboxylic acids.

questions.stem: Hell-Volard-Zelinsky reaction substitutes only
questions.explanation: HVZ substitutes the alpha-hydrogen of a carboxylic acid with a halogen.

questions.stem: In Hell-Volard-Zelinsky a catalytic amount of _____ is needed
questions.explanation: PBr3 (generated from P and Br2) is the catalyst in the HVZ reaction.

questions.stem: Which of these will reduce carboxylic acid to alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only LiAlH4 is strong enough to reduce carboxylic acids to primary alcohols.

questions.stem: ClCH2COOH is more acidic than CH3COOH by reason of
questions.explanation: The electron-withdrawing Cl atom exerts an inductive effect, stabilizing the anion and increasing acidity.

questions.stem: The periodic table is a chart that arranges elements according to
questions.explanation: The modern periodic table (Moseley's) arranges elements by increasing atomic number.

questions.stem: The principal use of diamond is in
questions.explanation: Diamond's hardness and brilliance make jewelry its principal use.

questions.stem: The ability of metals to conduct electricity is due to
questions.explanation: Metals conduct electricity because delocalized free electrons move through the metal lattice.

questions.stem: The reason why graphite is used as electrodes is due to

options.B: Presence of free mobile pi electrons

questions.explanation: Graphite has delocalized pi electrons that are free to move, making it an electrical conductor.

questions.stem: Which of these elements is NOT an alkaline-earth metal?
questions.explanation: Palladium (Pd) is a transition metal, not an alkaline-earth metal.

questions.stem: Which of these elements is NOT an alkali metal?
questions.explanation: Barium (Ba) is an alkaline-earth metal (Group 2), not an alkali metal (Group 1).

questions.stem: What is an alloy?

options.A: A miscible mixture of two or more metals at their molten states

questions.explanation: An alloy is a metallic mixture formed by combining metals in molten state.

questions.stem: Diamond has which hybridization?
questions.explanation: Each carbon in diamond is sp3 hybridized, forming four tetrahedral covalent bonds.

questions.stem: Is graphite convertible to diamond?
questions.explanation: At extremely high temperatures and pressures, graphite can be converted to diamond.

questions.stem: Which of these elements will liberate hydrogen from cold water?
questions.explanation: Potassium reacts with cold water: 2K + 2H2O -> 2KOH + H2.

questions.stem: Which of these elements will displace hydrogen from cold water?
questions.explanation: Rubidium is a very reactive alkali metal that reacts vigorously with cold water to liberate H2.

questions.stem: Group 18 elements like Ar, He, Ne and Kr are known as
questions.explanation: Group 18 elements have full outer shells and are chemically inert, called noble gases.

questions.stem: Group 17 elements like I, Br, F, Cl are known as
questions.explanation: Group 17 elements are halogens, highly electronegative nonmetals.

questions.stem: Which of these is a property of diamond?
questions.explanation: Diamond is the hardest naturally occurring substance.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a covalent crystal?
questions.explanation: Copper is a metallic crystal, not a covalent network solid.

questions.stem: Period 1 contains
questions.explanation: Period 1 contains only hydrogen (H) and helium (He).

questions.stem: Which of these materials is NOT a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Diamond has no free electrons; all are in strong covalent bonds, making it an insulator.

questions.stem: Transition elements are characterized by
questions.explanation: Transition metals have partially filled d subshells.

questions.stem: Which of these elements is NOT a transition metal?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is a halogen (Group 17), not a transition metal.

questions.stem: Lanthanides and Actinides have
questions.explanation: f-block elements have partially filled 4f or 5f orbitals.

questions.stem: The Mendeleev Periodic Table was based on
questions.explanation: Mendeleev arranged elements in order of increasing atomic mass.

questions.stem: Moseley's Periodic Table was rather based on
questions.explanation: Moseley showed that atomic number (not mass) is the fundamental organizing principle.

questions.stem: Noble gases have the following properties

options.B: No vacancies in their outermost s- or p-orbitals

questions.explanation: Noble gases have completely filled valence shells with no vacancies, making them chemically inert.

questions.stem: Which of these allotropes of carbon is most used as electrodes?
questions.explanation: Graphite is used as electrodes due to its mobile pi electrons enabling electrical conductivity.

questions.stem: What are hydrocarbons?

options.B: Compounds containing only carbon and oxygen
options.C: Compounds containing carbon, hydrogen and oxygen
options.D: Compounds containing only carbon and hydrogen

questions.explanation: Hydrocarbons are organic compounds composed exclusively of carbon and hydrogen.

questions.stem: In a molecule of a hydrocarbon with 5 carbon atoms, what is its formula if it is an alkyne?
questions.explanation: Alkynes: CnH(2n-2). For n=5: C5H8.

questions.stem: Which of the following will NOT give addition reactions: Propane, propyne, propene, benzene.
questions.explanation: Propane is a saturated alkane with no multiple bonds, so it does not undergo addition reactions.

questions.stem: An organic compound C2H6O oxidizes to compound B with same carbons, which further oxidizes to acetic acid. Compound A is
questions.explanation: Ethanol -> acetaldehyde -> acetic acid.

questions.stem: Products of reaction between ethanol and concentrated H2SO4 at 170°C?
questions.explanation: At 170°C, conc. H2SO4 dehydrates ethanol to ethene and water.

questions.stem: The combustion of a hydrocarbon will produce mandatory
questions.explanation: Complete combustion of any hydrocarbon always produces CO2.

questions.stem: Which substance presents only primary carbon atoms in its structure?
questions.explanation: Ethane (CH3-CH3) has only primary carbons.

questions.stem: What can result from the reduction of an aldehyde?
questions.explanation: Reduction of an aldehyde (RCHO) gives a primary alcohol (RCH2OH).

questions.stem: What can result from the reduction of a ketone?
questions.explanation: Reduction of a ketone (RCOR') gives a secondary alcohol.

questions.stem: The alcoholic fermentation is a reaction
questions.explanation: Alcoholic fermentation of glucose to ethanol is catalyzed by enzymes (zymase) in yeast.

questions.stem: An alkane with 10 carbon atoms is a _____ at room temperature.
questions.explanation: Alkanes with 5-17 carbons are liquids at room temperature. Decane (C10) is a liquid.

questions.stem: Alkanes react readily with
questions.explanation: Alkanes are very unreactive toward common reagents due to strong C-H and C-C bonds.

questions.stem: Which compound exhibits structural isomerism?
questions.explanation: Butane (C4H10) has two structural isomers: n-butane and isobutane.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an alcohol?
questions.explanation: CH3CH2OH (ethanol) contains the -OH functional group characteristic of alcohols.

questions.stem: What is meant by 'saturated' when describing hydrocarbons?

options.C: Saturated with hydrogens and have only single bonds between carbons

questions.explanation: Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) contain only C-C single bonds and the maximum number of hydrogens.

questions.stem: Which formula represents a saturated hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: C2H6 (ethane) fits the alkane formula CnH(2n+2) with only single bonds.

questions.stem: What characteristic is shared by all alkanes?
questions.explanation: All alkanes are flammable; they burn in oxygen to produce CO2 and H2O.

questions.stem: Straight chain alkenes have higher boiling point than isomeric branched chain compounds.
questions.explanation: Straight-chain alkenes have more surface area for van der Waals interactions.

questions.stem: What is the molecular formula of a compound with empirical formula CH2O and molar mass 180?
questions.explanation: Empirical mass 30; 180/30 = 6, so C6H12O6 (glucose).

questions.stem: Which of the following pollutants is biodegradable?
questions.explanation: Sewage compounds can be broken down by microorganisms.

questions.stem: To what temperature must a gas be raised from 273K to double both its volume and pressure?
questions.explanation: Using combined gas law: if P doubles and V doubles, T must quadruple: 4 x 273 = 1092K.

questions.stem: If 3 moles of electrons are required to deposit 1 mole of metal M, the empirical formula of its chloride is
